To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

UHRF 1 PHD finger acts together with the double Tudor domain of the adjacent region to recognize the H3 tail, and the preceding zinc-C4 knuckle is essential for the PHD of UHRF 2 PHD finger to bind to the histone H3N-terminal tail.

UHRF protein PHD finger (in complex with the preceding zinc-C4 knuckle) recognizes unmodified histone H3 and the double Tudor domain recognizes H3K9 methylated histone H3; the PHD finger (with zinc-C4 knucle) and the double Tudorfinger act together to specifically recognize H3K9m3 mark.
UHRF 1 double tudor and the adjacent PH D finger act together to specifically recognize H3K9 me3-containing histone tail, but not the unmodified histone tail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the PHD finger domain in UHRF1 protein.
the role of the PHD finger in UHRF1, which may help understand the mechanism of UHRF-mediated DNA methylation and its role in tumorigenesis.
the molecular mechanism of how UHRF1 recognizes the H3K4me3-containing histones and how UHRF2 binds to the H3K36me3-containing histoness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UHRF family proteins recognize the histone H3 K9me3 mark by the double Tudor domain in a cooperative manner with the adjacent PHD fingers.
the UHRF1 double Tudor domain and the PHD finger act in concert to specifically recognize K9me-containing histone H4 tail.
UHRF is a key epigenomic regulator that acts as a bridge between DNA methylation and histone methylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UHRF family proteins may be the only epigenetic regulators to have two different domains to specifically recognize H3K9 di- and trimethylated histone H3 tails.
the PHD finger and the Tudor domain of UHRF-1 act together to recognize H3K9 trimethylation.
UHRF protein has a unique architecture that is well suited for its function in maintaining DNA methylation and histone methylation patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UHRF1 double Tudor domain and the PHD finger act combinatorially to specifically recognize H3K9 methylated histone H3 tails.

UHRF is an epigenetic regulator that is able to bind to both methylated and unmodified H3 tail and that the UHRF protein can recognize the histone H3 methylated tail through the PHD finger and the Tudor domains.
UHRF proteins may act as a molecular switch to regulate the DNA methylation and histone H3 methylation patterns.
